Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

annual adjective

also yearly, once a year, an annual festival, lasting a year

classical

Verg. G. 1.338: annua magnae sacra refer Cererī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.16.5: quī creātur annuus

annuus, annua, annuum

adjective

yearly; lasting a year

Both senses of English annual: what comes round every year (annua sacra, the yearly rites) and what lasts a year (an office held for a year, Caes. BG 1.16.5). As a noun, annua (n. pl.) is a yearly allowance, a pension (see pension). Every year, as an adverb, is quotannīs (see every year).

Other words

  • anniversārius, anniversāria, anniversārium — coming round every year

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4, of rites and of feast days (Lewis & Short)

    Of what recurs at the same time each year: rites, feast days, the turn of the seasons. English anniversary comes from it; a birthday is diēs nātālis (see birthday).

Examples

  • tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum

    you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey by your monthly courseCatull. 34.17–18

  • quī summō magistrātuī praeerat, quem vergobretum appellant Haeduī, quī creātur annuus et vītae necisque in suōs habet potestātem

    who held the highest office, which the Haedui call the vergobret: he is elected for a year and has the power of life and death over his peopleCaes. BG 1.16.5

See also every year, year, pension, birthday.
